text:
jess: Quick API Q — we need to finalize the rerank response contract for the new unified scorer. Two main concerns: score semantics (range & meaning) and deterministic tie-breaking.

omar: TL;DR proposal in last PR: `score` = higher is better, unbounded float (can be -inf), plus `rank` integer is optional. We also suggested stable-sort by `id` for ties.

patrick: unbounded floats make client reasoning hard. Some clients expect 0..1. We should either normalize or provide both `score` and `confidence` (0..1).

jess: I prefer keeping raw `score` (model logit-like) and adding `confidence` 0..1 derived by softmax over returned candidates. That avoids breaking existing downstream math if they switch to rank.

omar: Agree. New response example:```json
{
  "request_id": "r-123",
  "items": [
    {"id":"doc:42","score": 12.34, "confidence": 0.72, "metadata": {...}},
    {"id":"doc:7","score": 12.34, "confidence": 0.20, "metadata": {...}},
    {"id":"doc:3","score": -5.1, "confidence": 0.08, "metadata": {...}}
  ]
}
```

lina: question: how do we compute confidence when only top-k are returned? softmax over top-k is fine but misleading for absolute certainties. We should call it `relative_confidence` or document behavior clearly.

jess: good point. call it `confidence` but in docs note: "confidence = softmax(scores) over returned items; not calibrated across different requests." Add `confidence_type` = "softmax_topk" to be explicit.

patrick: tie-breaking: stable sort by (`score` desc, `bias` secondary if present, then `id` lexicographic) — but if `score` identical due to quantization, we should allow an opt-in param `tie_breaker=round_robin` or `tie_breaker=deterministic`. Default=deterministic.

omar: Implementation note: runtime can attach `tie_reason` to each item when a secondary comparator was applied, e.g., "tie_reason":"id_lexicographic" so clients can audit.

infra-bot: deploy check: rerank-service v4.1 branch ready, feature-flag `rerank_v2_contract` off in prod.

jess: Backwards compatibility — current clients expecting `score` 0..1: we will not change existing hosted model responses. For dedicated/private, default config remains raw scores. We'll add `response_normalization= "none|softmax|minmax"` optional query param. Default remains `none`.

lina: docs action: I'll update OpenAPI with `confidence`, `confidence_type`, `tie_reason`, and param `response_normalization`. Also add example for `response_normalization=softmax`.

patrick: tests: add contract test validating (1) `items` order stable across repeated calls given same inputs, (2) `confidence` sums to ~1 when softmax used, (3) when `response_normalization=minmax`, `confidence` absent and `score` in [0,1].

omar: for customers with strict 0..1 needs, we add middleware that can rewrite responses to `score` 0..1 for a compatibility flag. Put migration docs in releases note.

jess: OK owners: lina -> OpenAPI + examples, patrick -> tests & tie-breaker unit tests, omar -> middleware & runtime flags. I'll add a short RFC doc and run a quick async review in #eng-platform.

lina: ping me on the PR for docs review. small nit: can we include `explain` optional string per item for server-side justification? useful for debug.

jess: yes `explain` optional string and `explain_tokens` optional small array for dedicated customers only. Add K/V size limit note.

omar: final ask — does anyone object to not bumping api version? My view: add fields non-breaking and keep same endpoint. If we add `response_normalization` param later default stays same.

patrick: no objection. add compatibility tests to ensure old clients still parse.

jess: Great. I'll capture action items in the RFC and tag owners. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder: please add feature flag rollback steps to the deploy playbook before merging.
